question: Built from a nitrogen-bearing sugar rather than plain glucose but linked the same β way, _____ stiffens the cuticle of every insect and the wall of every fungus.
questions: An insect can only grow by shedding its old cuticle, so it must carry enzymes that digest its own _____, and silencing one of them is lethal.
Second only to cellulose in abundance, _____ barely accumulates in marine sediments, because bacteria in the sea carry the enzymes to break it apart again.
abstract:
Chitin is a polysaccharide built from N-acetylglucosamine, a glucose ring carrying an acetylamino group, with the sugars joined end to end by β-1,4 glycosidic bonds. That β linkage is what makes cellulose a fibre rather than a store, and it does the same work here, holding the chains straight so they pack side by side instead of coiling. It is the structural material of fungal cell walls and of the cuticle of crustaceans and insects, and some algae build with it as well. Only cellulose is more abundant: the living world is estimated to make something on the order of a hundred billion tons of chitin a year. Almost none of it accumulates in marine sediments, because heterotrophic bacteria in the sea carry the enzymes to take it apart and return the carbon and nitrogen locked in it.

Because the material is rigid it cannot stretch, so an arthropod grows only by shedding it, which means digesting part of its own cuticle with chitinases it makes itself. In the pine sawyer beetle Monochamus alternatus, silencing one such enzyme, MaCht-2, caused molting failure, disordered cuticle ultrastructure, impaired movement and heavy mortality in larvae, pupae and adults alike. Animals that eat arthropods meet the same polymer from the other side, and mammals break it down with an enzyme called acidic mammalian chitinase. Across 37 rodent species the gene for it, CHIA, is often deleted or turned into a pseudogene in obligate herbivores whose food holds almost no chitin, and the strength of selection on it tracks how much of the diet is invertebrate. Chitin is also a signal the immune system watches for, and fungi such as Cryptococcus neoformans carry deacetylases that convert wall chitin into chitosan, which blunts the response that exposed chitin would provoke.
